= Use {ai-long} AI Functions
:page-component-name: cloud
:page-capella-type: AI
:page-topic-type: guide
:page-toclevels: 4
:description: Use AI Functions to summarize text, classify content, detect sentiment, explain patterns, and more — all within your {sqlpp} queries.

[abstract]
{description}

{ai-long} AI Functions combine {sqlpp} with language models to analyze your data.
Use large language models (LLMs) such as OpenAI, Bedrock, or models hosted in the xref:build:model-service/deploy-llm-model.adoc[{ai} Model Service] to run task-based functions using familiar {sqlpp} queries directly within Capella's query editor.

The following {ai} AI Functions are available:

* *Sentiment Analysis*: Determines text sentiment, such as positive, negative, neutral, or mixed.
* *Summarization*: Condenses lengthy text into key insights.
* *Classification*: Classifies data based on specified labels to improve organization and decision-making.
* *Entity Extraction*: Identifies user specified labels or entities. 
For example, you can extract entities such as persons, locations, organizations, and more from text or images.
* *Grammar Correction*: Fixes grammatical errors in the input text.
* *Text Generation*: Produces text from a prompt.
* *Masking*: Hides personally identifiable information (PII) like names and emails.
* *Similarity*: Compares texts and generates scores indicating how similar they are to each other.
* *Translation*: Converts text between languages.
* *Completion*: Allows you to define your own tasks using prompts and generates tailored responses. 
Combine with AI Guardrails for safe content generation. 

NOTE: When you use AI Functions, Capella charges based on your Model Service usage and Query Service usage.
If you're using external LLMs such as OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock, you incur charges from those model service providers. 

== Prerequisites

* You have deployed a xref:cloud:clusters:create-database.adoc[paid] Capella operational cluster with:

** Couchbase Server version 8.0 or later.
To upgrade your operational cluster, see xref:cloud:clusters:upgrade-database.adoc[].

** The xref:cloud:clusters:databases.adoc#couchbase-services[Query Service] enabled on 1 of your nodes. 

** The xref:cloud:billing:billing.adoc#dev-pro[Developer Pro] or xref:cloud:billing:billing.adoc#enterprise[Enterprise] Support Plan. 

** xref:cloud:clusters:databases.adoc#availability[Multiple Availability Zones] (AZ).

** A bucket with scopes, collections, and JSON documents.
For more information about how to upload data to Capella, see xref:cloud:guides:load.adoc[].
+
If you do not have a dataset, use the `travel-sample` dataset. 

* To enable and update AI Functions in the Capella UI, you need 1 of the following organization or project roles:

** xref:cloud:organizations:organization-user-roles.adoc#organization-role-organization-owner[`Organization Owner`]

** xref:cloud:projects:project-roles.adoc#project-owner-role[`Project Owner`]

** xref:cloud:projects:project-roles.adoc#project-cluster-manager-role[`Cluster Manager`]

** xref:cloud:projects:project-roles.adoc#project-cluster-data-reader-writer[`Data Writer`]

* To view and run AI Functions:

** In the Capella UI Query tab, you must have 1 of the following project roles:

*** xref:cloud:projects:project-roles.adoc#project-cluster-viewer-role[`Cluster Viewer`]

*** xref:cloud:projects:project-roles.adoc#project-cluster-data-reader[`Data Reader`]

** Your application must connect using 1 of the following types of cluster access credentials:

*** xref:cloud:clusters:cluster-rbac.adoc#basic-access-credentials[`Basic access credentials`]

*** xref:cloud:clusters:cluster-rbac.adoc#advanced-access-credentials[`Advanced access credentials`] assigned with a role that includes the `Query Curl Access` xref:cloud:clusters:cluster-rbac.adoc#privileges-for-advanced-access-credentials[privilege].

* A deployed LLM with:

** The xref:build:model-service/deploy-llm-model.adoc[{ai} Model Service]
** https://openai.com/[OpenAI^]
** https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/[Amazon Bedrock^]

* (Recommended) If you have a production workload, xref:security:add-aws-privatelink.adoc[enable private networking] to use AI Functions.
+
NOTE: If you want to enable private networking for your AI Functions, your {ai} model and Capella operational cluster need to be deployed within the same AWS region. 

* (Recommended) You have guardrails selected for your chosen model.
This includes keyword filtering and jailbreak detection. 
Guardrails are important to have when you use the completion function. 
For more information, see xref:build:model-service/deploy-llm-model.adoc[].

[#enable-ai-functions]
== Enable AI Functions

You can enable AI Functions on any of your Capella operational clusters.
Enabling AI Functions on 1 cluster does not automatically enable it on your other clusters.
You need to enable AI Functions individually for each cluster.

To enable {ai} AI Functions:

. Do 1 of the following:

.. Go to menu:{ai}[AI Functions].

.. On the *Operational* tab, click the name of the cluster where you want to enable AI Functions.

... Go to *AI Functions*.

. Click btn:[Enable AI Functions].

. Select the functions you want to use, and click btn:[Next].

. Select 1 of the model options:
+ 
NOTE: Private networking is only available for {ai} models. 

+
[{tabs}]
====
{ai} Model::
. Select *Capella Model*.
+
. Choose your {ai} model.
+
. Enter your *API Key ID* and *API Key Token*, or upload your `.txt` credentials file.
For more information about API keys for {ai} models, see xref:api-guide:api-start.adoc[].
+
. Click btn:[Next].
+
. Choose a Capella operational cluster for your functions.
+
. (Optional) If your {ai} model and your Capella operational cluster have the same AWS region, choose whether you want to enable private networking for your functions.
This enables private networking between your LLM's AWS region and your Capella operational cluster.
+
NOTE: You cannot disable private networking later. 

OpenAI Model::
. Select *OpenAI Model*.
+
. Choose your OpenAI model.
+
. (Optional) To use a new OpenAI API key, click btn:[Add New OpenAI API Key].
.. Click btn:[Add API Key]
.. Enter a name to identify your API Key in Capella.
.. Enter your *OpenAI API Key* from OpenAI.
.. Click btn:[Add Key].
+
. Choose your OpenAI API Key.
+
. Click btn:[Next].
+
. Choose a Capella operational cluster for your functions.

AWS Bedrock Model::
. Select *AWS Bedrock Model*.
+
. Enter your *Model ID* and choose your AWS *Region*.
+
. (Optional) To use a new Amazon Bedrock key, click btn:[New Bedrock Credentials].
.. Click btn:[Add Credentials]
.. Enter a name to identify your credential in Capella.
.. Enter your *Access Key ID* and *Secret Access Key* from Amazon Bedrock.
.. Click btn:[Add Credentials].
+
. Choose your Bedrock credentials.
+
. Click btn:[Next].
+
. Choose a Capella operational cluster for your functions.
====

. Click btn:[Complete Setup].

== Run an AI Function

Run AI Functions like any other {sqlpp} query using the xref:cloud:clusters:query-service/query-workbench.adoc[Query tab] on the operational cluster where you have configured AI Functions.

IMPORTANT: When using input prompts with {ai}, Bedrock, or OpenAI LLMs, turn on model guardrails for security.

Experiment with AI Functions with your own data or by loading a sample query into the Query tab of your operational cluster.
The following sample queries require the `travel-sample` dataset on the same cluster where you configured your AI Functions LLM.

For more information about how to load the `travel-sample` into your operational cluster, see xref:cloud:clusters:data-service/import-data-documents.adoc#import-sample-data[Import Sample Data].

To load a sample query:

. Copy a <<sample-queries,sample query>> from the list of {ai} AI Functions available. 
For example, copy the sample query for <<sentiment-analysis,>>.

. In your Capella operational cluster, go to menu:Data Tools[Query].

. In the query editor, replace the existing text with the sample query you copied. 

. Press kbd:[Enter] or click btn:[Run]. The query results are automatically displayed in JSON format.

Test these functions using your own data, queries, and prompts. 
You can specify a prompt in the {sqlpp} statement for prompt engineering to guide the LLM.
Use prompts to capture language, output format, examples, and other nuances that the LLM requires to perform these functions.

AI Function performance depends on the number and size of query nodes, data volume, and query complexity. 
Larger or more complex queries may require xref:cloud:clusters:scale-database.adoc[scaling your cluster] to maintain performance. 

NOTE: If you receive an error code `3000` after running your query, it indicates the function you're using is not enabled or associated with an LLM.
You need to <<enable-ai-functions,enable the function>> and try again.
For more information about {sqlpp} error codes, see xref:cloud:n1ql:n1ql-language-reference/n1ql-error-codes.adoc[]. 

== View AI Functions

To view a list of AI Functions in your organization and their associated operational clusters:

. Go to menu:{ai}[AI Functions].
. (Optional) Filter the list of AI Functions by their associated operational cluster, function name, and model service provider.

To view more details about the AI Functions associated with an operational cluster, do 1 of the following:

. Go to *Operational* and click the name of the cluster.
.. Go to *AI Functions*.
. From menu:{ai}[AI Functions], click the name of an operational cluster.

You can view the status of each of your AI Functions and <<change-model-association,change their associated model>>.
Click the name of the associated model to get more information. 

The status of your AI Function can be dependent on the status of its associated model.
An AI function can have 1 of the following statuses:

|====
| Status | Description

| Healthy
a| The model associated to your AI Functions is in a healthy state. 

| Unhealthy
a| The model associated to your AI Functions is in an unhealthy state.

| Deploying
a| After you enable your AI Functions, they enter a deploying state. 

This may take some time.
You can use your AI Functions when the status changes to *Healthy*. 

| Deployment Failed
a| Your AI Functions failed to deploy. 

| Updating
a| Your AI Functions are updating after you changed the associated model. 

This may take some time.
You can use your AI Functions when the status changes to *Healthy*. 
|====
